haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: the write commits to MySQL with an outbox row, then an inline copy goes to Postgres with a 200 ms timeout. If Postgres fails or times out, the request still succeeds and the outbox row waits for the relay.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming row's version is higher than the Postgres row's version. Equal or higher versions are never overwritten, and ids with a tombstone are never written.
haiku-low.q3: Step 4 gate: app_flag_value users_dual_write is 1 on every instance, and app_build_info shows the release version on every instance. Instances can disagree for up to 30 s after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: It reads at most 2,000 rows per batch from the replica, waits while replica lag is unknown or above 5 s, pauses 100 ms between batches, and one leader holds the users_backfill lock.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: backfill done, outbox empty, a full sweep passed, and a full comparison with zero mismatches. Source switch: 3-day soak at 100% reads, outbox empty, normal replica lag, comparison within 24 hours with zero mismatches.
haiku-low.q6: The MySQL outbox table users_sync_outbox, written in the same transaction as the change. The single relay (GET_LOCK) drains it to Postgres once it is back. The sweep also repairs differences.
haiku-low.q7: Copies and erasure take the same Postgres advisory lock per id. Copies skip tombstoned ids and erasure writes a tombstone, so a copy that lands first is deleted and a later copy is skipped.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is cursor_id in users_backfill_state in pg-core, updated in the same Postgres transaction as the copied rows, so it is never ahead of the data. It is marked done when finished; the document gives no other stop rule.
haiku-low.q9: The sweep (step 6) compares 2,000-id hash chunks and re-checks MySQL primary. Newer or missing MySQL rows are copied. Postgres-only rows with no pending outbox row are deleted with a tombstone. A higher Postgres version is never overwritten; it alerts.
haiku-low.q10: Writes pause (mode paused). The commit point takes MySQL's users_migration lock exclusively and sets sot=pg, so late MySQL writers get 503. Drain limit is 20 s, alert at 75 s, hard limit 90 s. Crashes after (c) need manual roll-forward.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns new ids after the switch, from users_id_seq set to max id plus 1,000,000. MySQL assigns no ids in pg mode, and reverse copies keep Postgres ids. MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set past both maxima only on rollback.
haiku-low.q12: Writes in pg mode also add reverse outbox rows, copied inline and by a reverse relay to MySQL, including erasures and tombstones. Rollback is the step 11 runbook: pause, drain, commit in Postgres, set MySQL sot back. The option ends 14 days after step 10e.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first (commit with the outbox row in the same transaction), then copied to Postgres inline after commit (200 ms timeout). If the Postgres part fails or times out, the request still succeeds and the outbox row stays for the relay.
sonnet.q2: Only when the existing Postgres row's version is lower than the incoming version (and the id has no tombstone). Never on equal or higher version.
sonnet.q3: app_flag_value{flag="users_dual_write"} must be 1 on every instance and app_build_info must show the release version on every instance (flag alone not enough). Instances can disagree for up to 30 s (flag cache reload interval).
sonnet.q4: It checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds before each batch (waits 5 s if unknown or above 5 s), reads from the replica in batches of at most 2,000 rows, and waits 100 ms after each commit so reporting jobs can use the replica.
sonnet.q5: Reads: a full comparison with zero mismatches (backfill done, outbox empty, one full sweep passed). Source of truth move: reads 100% on Postgres for at least 3 days (soak), outbox empty, replica lag normal, and a full comparison within the last 24 h with zero mismatches.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox) in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the users write, records it. The relay copies outbox rows to Postgres (and the sweep repairs anything missed).
sonnet.q7: Tombstones: erasure writes a tombstone (id, erased_at) in Postgres users_tombstones, and every copy takes the per-id Postgres advisory lock and skips tombstoned ids. A copy that commits first is removed by the delete; one that starts later sees the tombstone and is skipped.
sonnet.q8: In users_backfill_state (cursor_id) in pg-core. The cursor is updated in the same Postgres transaction as the batch data, so it is never ahead of the data. It stops when users_backfill_state is done (reaching the end of the ids; the document does not describe the exact end condition beyond status done).
sonnet.q9: The continuous repair sweep compares chunks of 2,000 ids by fingerprint and re-reads mismatches on the MySQL primary (checking the outbox first). If MySQL has a newer or missing row it copies with the version rule; if Postgres has a row MySQL lacks with no pending outbox row, it deletes it and writes a tombstone; if Postgres has a higher version it never overwrites and alerts.
sonnet.q10: Writes are paused (mode paused, all instances report paused), outbox drained, then a commit point in MySQL takes the exclusive lock on users_migration and sets sot='pg' with epoch+1. App writes hold the shared lock and check the control row (fence), so a lagging instance either commits before (c) or gets a 503. Reverse copies run only when sot='pg'. If the drain takes more than 20 s the mode goes back to mysql and nothing has changed; alert at 75 s, hard limit 90 s; after (c) it rolls forward manually (open question: crash could exceed 90 s).
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids via users_id_seq, set with setval to GREATEST(max id on both)+1,000,000 and made the column default. Reverse copies carry the Postgres id to MySQL. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set past both maxima (step 11d).
sonnet.q12: Each Postgres write inserts a reverse outbox row and is copied to MySQL inline (200 ms timeout), with the reverse relay copying the rest (reverse sync). Rollback is the step 10 runbook with roles swapped: reads to mysql, pause writes, drain reverse outbox (20 s limit), commit point in Postgres (sot='mysql', epoch+1), then fix AUTO_INCREMENT, set MySQL control row, turn reverse sync off, set mode mysql. The option ends at step 13, at least 14 days after step 10e, when reverse sync is turned off and app write privileges on MySQL users are revoked (MySQL table dropped at least 7 days later).
